endorsements.quote: Therefore, while LLMs show great promise in clinical workflows, they should augment, rather than replace, physician-led care ( Table 1 ).
Furthermore, ensuring that physicians are actively involved in the development and evaluation of LLMs for health care is essential in keeping with a physician-led approach.

Clinical use cases of LLMs are already being tested; delaying collaboration among all stakeholders, including health care professionals, ethicists, AI researchers, and (crucially) patients, will only delay the discovery of potential harms.
Real-world pilots, therefore, should be deployed alongside regular monitoring, oversight, and feedback from all parties.

unlisted_practices: Regulators should develop robust regulatory frameworks and expeditious guidelines for software as a medical device that enable continuous evaluation of evolving LLM technology.
Regulatory bodies should implement risk-benefit calculations and a regulatory framework before LLMs are permitted in clinical care until systematic evaluation of LLM biases is performed.
Design artificial empathy in LLMs to complement rather than replace human empathy.
Professional societies should develop and continuously update guidelines for equitable use of LLMs in health care.
Professional societies should allocate grant funding to projects that use LLMs to ameliorate inequities.
Journals should prioritize publications on novel methods and use-case comparisons of LLMs for equitable care delivery.
Add human verification steps at both the input and output stages of LLM-guided generation of clinical texts.
Incorporate a systematized, frequently reevaluated method of bias evaluation into clinical applications of LLMs.
Use diverse training data sources and continuous bias evaluation in LLM development.
Conduct ethical evaluations together with evaluation of use case efficacy for LLMs.
Software developers and industry should collaborate with health care workers on model improvement strategies that improve health equity.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/framework paper presenting ethical considerations and frameworks for empathy and equity in LLM deployment rather than an empirical study.
